title: When WordPress Is Appropriate and When a Static Site Is Better

cover.alt: Concept illustration of a modular publishing workstation and a prebuilt-page delivery workstation, presented as equally valid choices.

figures.title: Choose around the team's workflow
figures.summary: Match the platform to editing habits, functionality, and ongoing support.

items.label: Frequent nontechnical editing
items.detail: A WordPress dashboard may suit a team that needs to publish directly.

items.label: Mostly fixed content
items.detail: A static build may suit occasional developer-managed changes.

items.label: Required functionality
items.detail: Compare suitable plugins with the integrations or custom work a static approach needs.

items.label: Ongoing ownership
items.detail: Identify who will maintain updates, backups, deployments, and external services.

figures.caption: A decision framework from the article, not a blanket performance or security rating.

figures.title: Migration includes more than page text
figures.summary: Preserve the useful content and behavior when changing how the site is delivered.

items.label: Export
items.detail: Retrieve the WordPress content and collect its media files.

items.label: Convert
items.detail: Map the content into the new format and repair image references.

items.label: Preserve destinations
items.detail: Keep useful slugs and map changing URLs to their new locations.

items.label: Transfer metadata
items.detail: Carry relevant titles and descriptions into the new content model.

items.label: Rebuild interactions
items.detail: Replace plugin-dependent forms and verify their complete flow.

figures.caption: The article's migration checklist. Scope and timing depend on the content and integrations involved.
